title: USS Hornet Ranked as one of California's 10 Most Haunted Places
excerpt: Halloween is right around the corner—and you won’t have to travel far to check out one of the most haunted places in California. The USS Hornet is leaning into their reputation as the fourth most haunted location in California with partying, sipping, spooking, and scaring all month long.
content:
Halloween is right around the corner—and you won’t have to travel far to check out one of the most haunted places in California, according to the latest HauntBound index. The USS Hornet, right here in Alameda, ranks #4 among California’s 10 most haunted places.

The HauntBound travel site, which ranks 554 haunted places in the state according to published accounts, includes 13 separate accounts of the haunted Hornet, the most of any in California. The Essex-class ship was commissioned on November 29, 1943, and recovered the Apollo 11 and Apollo 12 astronauts in 1969. Reports of ghostly figures seen aboard the ship most often involve young men in 1940s-era sailing uniforms, observed in the enlisted crew quarters, the chief petty officers’ mess, the aft elevator, the brig, and the engine room.

“The CPO mess produces the most-cited single reports,” HauntBound reports, “with multiple visitors and staff describing figures seated at the mess tables or moving between the galley pass-through and the seating area. The aft elevator has produced reports of mechanical activation when the elevator should be locked and inoperable.”

These reports are not just legends, according to the HauntBound site. “We rank by evidence, not legend,” said Ben Fineman, the website’s editor. “The ranking shows each site’s documented record—independent published accounts, documented history, and how far back the reports go. We don’t claim ghosts are real, or that they aren’t. We document where the reports concentrate, and we show our work.”

The San Francisco Ghosts website stated that the USS Hornet “is acknowledged as the most haunted Navy ship in America.” And it’s not just ghost-travel companies that report on the USS Hornet’s spooky visitors.

“Paranormal enthusiasts from near and far have come to spend the night in the original sailors’ bunks and set up ghost-detecting instruments in some of the ship’s deepest compartments,” KQED News reported in an October 2024 episode of Bay Curious.

“In the Hornet’s sick bay, rows of WWII-era hospital beds with white sheets and metal frames stretched back into shadowed corners,” the KQED report continued. “Faye Navarro, private events manager on the USS Hornet, placed a small, coffin-shaped box on one of the beds—a motion-detecting music box used to sense the presence of spirits. ‘When you’re looking down, and this thing is going off, and you don’t see anybody, it gets creepy,’ Navarro said.”

Navarro and fellow tour guide Steve Jackson told KQED they used pendulums, dowsing rods, and even Maglite flashlights, to try to communicate with the ghosts. “The theory is that spirits are able to bridge the gap between the battery and the light to be able to answer questions,” Jackson said. “But sadly, they can only answer yes-or-no questions.”

Is the Hornet really haunted? “Depends on who you ask,” according to a Veteran Life report, which notes that Caltech has created a catalog of ghost stories about experiences aboard the ship “that have ranged from misunderstandings to the unexplainable.”

Want to see for yourself?

The USS Haunted Hornet: The Devil’s Sea | Running regularly Sunday, November 1: The USS Hornet Sea, Air & Space Museum has teamed up with Dead Time Dreams Haunted Attractions to create a frightening and fascinating haunted house experience. Grab a drink from The Fireside Lounge’s “The Devil’s Tavern” on select evenings for “haunted mocktails, eerie elixirs, and chilling non-alcoholic drinks.” Get your tickets online.

Ship of Spirits: Spaghetti & Spirits Paranormal Dinner and Tour | Thursday, October 23, from 7 to 11:30 p.m.: Join the Hornet crew for a traditional spaghetti dinner and discussion of the Hornet’s reported paranormal activity. The crew will share experiences and evidence of the legendary hauntings onboard, followed by an exclusive 30-minute presentation by the Angels of Light Paranormal Society (ALPS). Bring a flashlight for a spooky “flashlight tour” after dinner. Grab your tickets online.

Monster Bash 2026 | Saturday, October 24, from 8 p.m. to 1 a.m.: Get ready for the Hornet’s big Halloween bash with live music, a dance floor, and no host bars. Enter the costume contest for a chance to win $300. STARMAN, a David Bowie tribute band, will keep you out of your seat all night. Grab your tickets for the Monster Bash online. If you’d like to double dip the fun that evening, use the Haunted Hornet ticket website to reserve a slot at the Haunted Hornet attraction, and then select the “Haunted Hornet + Monster Bash Combo.” You’ll save on processing fees by purchasing them together.

Meanwhile, check out the USS Hornet History Mystery Tours, which run year round:

  • Thursday, October 15 (Info & tickets).
  • Friday, October 16 (Info & tickets).
  • Halloween! Saturday, October 31 (Info & tickets).
  • Friday, November 13 (Info & tickets).
  • Thursday, December 3 (Info & tickets).

The USS Hornet is located at 707 West Hornet Avenue. It is open Wednesday through Sunday for self-guided visits; tickets for evening and overnight paranormal programs must be purchased in advance.
